evidence: Receiving DO2 time series: 10.75 mg/L at 48.0 h collapsing to 2.43 (48.2 h), 2.15 (50.0 h), 1.64 mg/L (52.0 h) — below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen constraint
Receiving delayed P assays: 0 g/L @24 h, 1.03 g/L @36 h, 3.04 g/L @48 h — active production, stop would forfeit ~3 g/L inventory
Source batches never fell below ~7.4 mg/L DO2 — receiving oxygen-transfer deficit is process-specific, not a source trait

Forward model comparison at t=52 h: strong_feed_reduction min DO 1.13 mg/L, deficit 4.32 mg·h/L, mass 172.3 kg; superior to combined (0.96 / 6.88 / 171.4), increase_air (0.87 / 8.63 / 171.3), reduce_feed (0.85 / 8.67 / 171.3)
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 fell from ~10.7 mg/L at 48.0 h to 2.4 mg/L at 48.2 h and 1.64 mg/L at 52.0 h, below the 2.0 mg/L oxygen minimum, indicating feed-driven oxygen demand exceeding transfer capacity while product continues to accumulate (P = 3.04 g/L at 48 h). Source batches show the same trajectory shape but with a weaker DO dip (min ~8 mg/L), confirming a receiving-specific transfer shortfall. Among the bounded interventions, the nominal source-calibrated forward model ranks strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) best on both oxygen recovery (post-decision minimum DO 1.13 mg/L, oxygen deficit 4.32 mg·h/L vs 6.9-8.7 for alternatives) and product mass (172.3 kg vs ~171.3-171.4 kg). Stop is rejected because it counts zero production despite a healthy 3+ g/L inventory. Though the nominal model flags even this action as borderline on the oxygen constraint, strong feed reduction offers the largest safety margin and the sensitivity ensemble (min DO up to 1.72) shows feasibility is achievable in favorable parameter realizations; it is the only option that both relieves oxygen limitation and retains product mass.
args.uncertainty: The nominal forward model is source-calibrated and imperfect for the receiving process (estimated transfer multiplier 0.43); even the best action is predicted to leave DO below 2.0 mg/L for ~8.4 h post-decision, so full constraint compliance is not guaranteed. The sensitivity ensemble (min DO 0.73-1.72) suggests outcomes could improve materially or remain violated. The delayed P assay is 4 h stale; current biomass/OUR could be higher than assumed, worsening the deficit. The abrupt DO step at 48.2 h could partly reflect a sensor or air-supply event rather than purely metabolic demand; if so, feed reduction would over-correct and sacrifice some production.
